diagnostic_evidence.quote: can treat general $\mathcal{F}_T$-measurable square-integrable terminal conditions. We provide a complete convergence analysis with respect to all discretization and truncation parameters
Throughout the section, we also assume that the generator $f$ is deterministic

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and conclusion pair 'arbitrary/general square-integrable terminal conditions' with a 'comprehensive/complete' convergence analysis. Every convergence statement depends on the Euler rate theorem, which requires $\xi\in\mathbb{D}^{2,q}$, $q>4$, Hölder-continuous Malliavin derivatives, and $f\in C^{1:2}_b$. The bounds also contain $\mathbb{E}\|D\xi\|^2$, which is infinite for general $L^2$ data. The analysis further assumes deterministic $f$ and $d=1$. The discontinuous barrier payoff in Example 1 is not Malliavin differentiable, so it lies outside the theory, as does the non-differentiable generator of Example 3. The paper therefore proves convergence only for Malliavin-smooth terminal conditions, not for general $L^2$ ones.

failure_location.quote: our approach accommodates arbitrary $\mathcal{F}_T$-measurable square-integrable terminal conditions. We provide a comprehensive convergence analysis

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the convergence claims to terminal conditions and generators satisfying Assumption 2.3 (and deterministic $f$, $d=1$). State that implementability, not proven convergence, extends to general $L^2$ data.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed convergence guarantee for general $L^2$ (path-dependent, non-smooth) terminal conditions, the paper's main selling point, is unsupported. The numerical examples are not covered by the theory.
issues.title: Convergence analysis advertised for arbitrary square-integrable terminal conditions
issues.why_classification: The rewording is easy, but it removes an advertised regime: proven convergence for arbitrary square-integrable terminal conditions. A comparable result survives only for smooth data.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the $n$th Wiener chaos when truncating the basis $(h_{j})_{j\geq 1}$ to $M$ elements

issues.failure_explanation: $D_s\mathcal{C}^{P,M}(F)$ projects each kernel $g_n$ onto the span of $h_1,\dots,h_M$ in all $n$ variables, including the variable $s$. In contrast, $\mathcal{C}^{P-1,M}(D_sF)$ leaves $s$ unprojected. Counterexample: take $F=B(h)$ with $h\perp h_1,\dots,h_M$. Then $\mathcal{C}^{1,M}(F)=0$, so $D_s\mathcal{C}^{1,M}(F)=0$, while $\mathcal{C}^{0,M}(D_sF)=h(s)\neq0$. The identity is false, and it is stated without proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second identity in (ii) with the norm inequality $\mathbb{E}\|D^k\mathcal{C}^{P,M}F\|^2\le\mathbb{E}\|D^kF\|^2$. This follows from Lemma 'lemma norm malliavin' and $\mathbb{E}|\mathcal{P}^{n,M}F|^2\le\mathbb{E}|\mathcal{P}^nF|^2$.
issues.overall_effect: Part (ii) of the lemma is false for truncated bases. Its only use, the bound $\mathbb{E}\|D\mathcal{C}^{\theta(m)}\xi\|^2\le\mathbb{E}\|D\xi\|^2$, remains true by another argument.
issues.title: False commutation of Malliavin derivative with basis-truncated chaos projection
issues.why_classification: A short local replacement supplies everything the paper actually uses. No downstream claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: By the scheme's definition, the right-hand side is $\mathcal{C}^{\theta(i)}(F_i^{\pi,\theta})=Y_{t_i}^{\pi,\theta}+\Delta_i\mathcal{C}^P(f_i^{\pi,\theta})$, not $F_i^{\pi,\theta}$. The recursion as written therefore differentiates an identity that does not hold. Separately, the proof needs $|\pi|\le\min(1,\epsilon)$ and $\xi\in\mathbb{D}^{1,2}$, but neither appears in the lemma statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate the correct identity. Use $\mathbb{E}\|D\mathcal{C}^P(f_i)\|^2\le\mathbb{E}\|Df_i\|^2$ (via the chaos norm formula), and add $\xi\in\mathbb{D}^{1,2}$ and small mesh to the hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of the P-uniform Malliavin energy bound used in Theorem 4.? (thm:added-4) is invalid. The bound itself is recoverable.
issues.title: Energy estimate differentiates the wrong backward identity and omits its mesh condition
issues.why_classification: The repair is local, using one contraction inequality and explicit hypotheses. The same recursion and constants survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The $C|\pi|$ term comes from Theorem 'Theorem main convergence rate', which requires Assumption 2.3 ($\xi\in\mathbb{D}^{2,q}$, Hölder Malliavin derivatives, $f\in C^{1:2}_b$, time-Hölder $f$) and $|\pi|<\eta$. The $P$-uniform term uses Lemma 'lem:malliavin-energy', which needs $f\in C^{1:1}_b$ and $\xi\in\mathbb{D}^{1,2}$. Both main theorems are stated under Assumption 1 and mesh regularity only. Under these hypotheses the $|\pi|$ rate is not established, and $\mathbb{E}\|D\xi\|^2$ may be infinite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add Assumption 2.3 (which gives $f\in C^{1:1}_b$ and $\xi\in\mathbb{D}^{1,2}$) and the condition $|\pi|<\eta$, small enough for the lemmas, to the hypotheses of both theorems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notice that for a general square-integrable random variable $F$, the quantity $\mathbf{V}_i (F)$ can still be infinite.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1 only requires $\xi\in L^2$, which does not imply fourth moments. Finiteness of $\mathbf{V}_m(\xi)$ needs $\mathbb{E}(\xi^2H_a^2)<\infty$, which can fail for $L^2$ variables, as the paper itself admits. The remark thus contradicts the paper's own observation.

failure_location.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption 1}, the random variable $\xi$ has absolute moments of fourth order, and hence $\mathbf{V}_{m}(\xi)$ can be proven to be finite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require $\xi\in L^{q}$ with $q>4$ (implied by Assumption 2.3), or assume $\mathbf{V}_m(\xi)<\infty$ explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The Monte Carlo bound of thm:added-5 may be vacuous ($C_{P,M}=\infty$) under the stated assumptions, contrary to the remark.
issues.title: False claim that Assumption 1 gives fourth moments and finite V_m(xi)
issues.why_classification: Replacing the cited assumption with an available stronger one restores the claim without changing any result.
